label: Game B
nuance_found: The lantern dial is the whole game: low tide to cross causeways and sand bars, high tide to float Tam's boat and the raft, and a mid band to steer the boat through the Needles. The Undertow boss needed a sequence (lure it with high water, strand it with low water, slam the sea back up, then shine) three times, and the crab got warier each round.
audio: Ambient wind loop, a short soft chime when the lantern moves, location jingles, a boss sting and a finale piece; mostly calm and quiet, with a little music.
furthest_progress: Finished the main story at about 5 min: Gullwick Harbour, Well Islet shard, floated Tam's boat, the Shellflats raft and the keeper's lens, sailed the Needles, beat the Undertow boss (3 knocks), and lit the lamp on the Stack for the end card ('0 of 5 lost things found'). After that I only wandered at night.
control_trouble: Walking and steering a boat by blind lantern drags was fiddly with 0.5 s looks; I leaned on the walk assist for almost all travel. Dialog boxes also covered the lantern, so two of my drags missed.
best_moment: Raising the sea and watching the raft lift me up to the wreck, then beating the giant crab with the tide.
worst_moment: After the finale the game told me nothing to do, there were 5 lost things I had no clue how to find, and wandering the dark island was empty.
verdict: A pretty, cosy little adventure with one clever trick: you move the sea with a thumb, and the sea changes what you can reach. It teaches that quickly and every few minutes it gave me something new, a floating raft, a boat through rocks, a crab boss. It is a bit story-and-walking heavy for a bus ride and I had no way to see the 'lost things', but it is a nicer surprise than most games I try. It ended in about five minutes, which is short but satisfying.
